checkpoints.question: An IDOR vulnerability occurs when an application fails to check what before exposing an internal resource to a user?

options.A: whether the user's browser supports the protocol
options.B: whether the user is authenticated to the system
options.C: whether the user is authorized to access that specific resource
options.D: whether the user's IP address is on the allowlist

checkpoints.explanation: IDOR happens when an app exposes a reference to an internal resource without checking if the requesting user is authorized to access that specific resource. Authentication alone is not sufficient.

checkpoints.question: Which technique do attackers use to bypass naive filters when performing directory traversal attacks?

options.A: URL encoding to represent path separator characters differently
options.B: modifying the Host header to redirect file paths
options.C: sending multiple requests with random timing intervals
options.D: injecting comments into the file path parameter

checkpoints.explanation: Attackers bypass naive filters by using URL encoding—representing characters as percent-encoded values like %2e%2e%2f instead of ../ to avoid simple string matching.

checkpoints.question: In a cloud environment, why is the instance metadata service at 169.254.169.254 considered a high-value SSRF target?

options.A: it filters and validates all outbound network traffic
options.B: it enforces mandatory encryption on all requests
options.C: it contains the source code of all running applications
options.D: it exposes credentials and configuration data for the instance

checkpoints.explanation: The instance metadata service at 169.254.169.254 is a link-local address that exposes credentials and configuration for the cloud VM, making it an attractive SSRF target in cloud environments.

checkpoints.question: What is the root cause of command injection vulnerabilities?

options.A: the application uses encrypted communication channels
options.B: the application does not separate data from commands
options.C: the application logs all user input to a file
options.D: the application runs with administrative privileges

checkpoints.explanation: Command injection occurs because the application does not separate data from commands, allowing shell metacharacters in user input to be interpreted as command syntax rather than literal data.

checkpoints.question: How does an XXE attack exploit vulnerable XML parsers?

options.A: by sending XML in an unsupported encoding format
options.B: by declaring external entities that reference files or URLs
options.C: by removing the XML declaration from the document header
options.D: by overloading the parser with large XML documents

checkpoints.explanation: XXE exploits XML parsers that honor external entity references embedded in the document, allowing attackers to declare entities pointing to sensitive files like /etc/passwd or internal URLs.

checkpoints.question: LDAP injection attacks and SQL injection attacks follow the same basic principle but target different systems. Which system does LDAP injection target?
checkpoints.explanation: LDAP injection targets applications that build LDAP queries by concatenating unsanitized user input. LDAP is used to query directory services like Active Directory.

checkpoints.question: Why can CSRF attacks succeed even when the victim is legitimately logged into the target web application?

options.A: browsers attach session cookies to requests regardless of origin
options.B: authentication tokens are stored in local storage publicly
options.C: the attacker can intercept and modify the session cookie
options.D: web applications cannot validate the origin of requests

checkpoints.explanation: CSRF succeeds because browsers automatically attach session cookies to every request for a domain, regardless of where the request originates, so the victim's valid session is used without their knowledge.

checkpoints.question: What does a clickjacking attack place over a visible, legitimate page to trick victims into triggering unintended actions?

options.A: a pop-up window with misleading text or content
options.B: a hidden form embedded in the page source code
options.C: an invisible or transparent iframe containing a malicious target
options.D: a JavaScript alert box asking for user confirmation

checkpoints.explanation: Clickjacking overlays an invisible or transparent iframe containing a malicious target over a visible, legitimate page, so victims click what they see but trigger what they cannot.

checkpoints.question: How does a session fixation attack typically compromise an authenticated session?

options.A: the attacker steals the session ID from network traffic
options.B: the attacker uses brute force to guess the session ID
options.C: the attacker pre-establishes a session ID and tricks the victim into using it
options.D: the attacker modifies the session timeout value on the server

checkpoints.explanation: Session fixation occurs when the attacker pre-establishes a known session ID, tricks the victim into authenticating with that same ID, then uses it to access the now-authenticated session.

checkpoints.question: What is the difference between horizontal and vertical privilege escalation in web applications?

options.A: horizontal exploits network vulnerabilities; vertical exploits application logic
options.B: horizontal accesses other users at the same level; vertical gains higher-privilege functions
options.C: horizontal requires authentication; vertical does not require authentication
options.D: horizontal targets databases; vertical targets file systems

checkpoints.explanation: Horizontal escalation accesses resources of other users at the same privilege level, while vertical escalation gains access to higher-privilege functions or data that a user should not have.

checkpoints.question: Why is deserialization of untrusted data dangerous?

options.A: it prevents applications from caching frequently accessed objects
options.B: it increases the time required to process user requests
options.C: it requires excessive memory and causes denial of service
options.D: serialization formats allow data to specify object types, enabling code execution

checkpoints.explanation: Deserialization becomes dangerous when untrusted data specifies the object type and parameters to instantiate, allowing attackers to craft payloads that trigger arbitrary code execution.
